```{python}
#| label: fig-stdcell-layout
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Typical layout organization of a standard cell (shown: an inverter): fixed cell height with horizontal $V_\\mathrm{DD}$/$V_\\mathrm{SS}$ rails in `M1` at top and bottom, the n-well with the PMOS in the upper half, the NMOS in the lower half, a shared vertical poly gate as input, and the output on `M1`."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pyutil import laygen as lg

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4.6))

# n-well upper half
lg.rect(ax, 'NW', -0.6, 3.4, 6.8, 3.4)
# power rails merged with the source stubs (one polygon per supply net)
lg.poly(ax, 'M1', [(-0.6, 7.0), (6.2, 7.0), (6.2, 6.2), (2.15, 6.2),
                   (2.15, 4.55), (1.45, 4.55), (1.45, 6.2), (-0.6, 6.2)])
lg.poly(ax, 'M1', [(-0.6, -0.8), (6.2, -0.8), (6.2, 0.0), (2.15, 0.0),
                   (2.15, 1.45), (1.45, 1.45), (1.45, 0.0), (-0.6, 0.0)])
# PMOS active + BP
lg.rect(ax, 'BP', 1.0, 3.9, 3.6, 2.0)
lg.rect(ax, 'RX', 1.4, 4.2, 2.8, 1.4)
# NMOS active
lg.rect(ax, 'RX', 1.4, 0.6, 2.8, 1.1)
# shared poly gate
lg.rect(ax, 'PC', 2.55, 0.0, 0.5, 6.1)
# contacts
lg.contacts(ax, 1.6, 4.7, 1, 1, size=0.4)
lg.contacts(ax, 3.7, 4.7, 1, 1, size=0.4)
lg.contacts(ax, 1.6, 0.9, 1, 1, size=0.4)
lg.contacts(ax, 3.7, 0.9, 1, 1, size=0.4)
# output connection (single strip: PMOS drain to NMOS drain)
lg.rect(ax, 'M1', 3.55, 0.75, 0.7, 4.5)
# input pin marker
lg.contacts(ax, 2.6, 2.6, 1, 1, size=0.4)
lg.rect(ax, 'M1', 2.45, 2.45, 0.7, 0.7)

ax.text(6.5, 6.6, '$V_\\mathrm{DD}$ rail', fontsize=8, va='center')
ax.text(6.5, -0.4, '$V_\\mathrm{SS}$ rail', fontsize=8, va='center')
ax.text(6.5, 4.9, 'PMOS', fontsize=8, va='center')
ax.text(6.5, 1.1, 'NMOS', fontsize=8, va='center')
ax.text(2.8, -1.4, 'input (poly)', fontsize=8, ha='center')
ax.text(4.6, 3.0, 'output', fontsize=8)

lg.finish(ax, (-1.0, 9.4), (-1.8, 7.6))
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
